name: Amtrak at Tampa Union Station
summary: Tampa's Amtrak station, an Italian Renaissance-style building that opened in May 1912, is served by the Floridian, which Amtrak describes as a temporary combination of the Capitol Limited and Silver Star running daily between Chicago and Miami via Washington, DC.
notes: Amtrak's pages were read through WebFetch only (amtrak.com refuses curl). Verified 2026-09-27: the Floridian page's alert reads 'Service Adjustments South of Washington, DC. Effective October 16 - 26, 2026', caused by the East River Tunnel rehabilitation in New York; the Silver Star page says the Silver Star is temporarily combined into the Floridian. Station hours were not shown. Visit Tampa Bay's transportation page says the train connects Tampa with New York, Philadelphia, Washington, Orlando and Miami, but the Amtrak pages read describe the Floridian as Chicago-Miami, so that claim is not repeated. Point is the OpenStreetMap station building; the stop links the history-tampa place tampa-union-station.

name: Anna Maria Island Trolley (MCAT Route 5)
fare_text: Free.
hours_text: 6:00 a.m.-10:30 p.m. every day, 365 days a year; every 20 minutes.
summary: A free Manatee County trolley along Gulf Drive on Anna Maria Island between the Anna Maria City Pier and Coquina Beach, every 20 minutes from 6 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. daily. MCAT trolleys are wheelchair accessible and carry bike racks.
notes: Real-time arrivals are in Manatee County's MyStop app. Stop points are OpenStreetMap features (the Anna Maria City Pier and the 'COQUINA BEACH' bus stop). Verified 2026-09-27: county page re-read; free, 6:00am-10:30pm, 365 days, every 20 minutes, bike racks on all buses and trolleys.

name: Central Avenue Trolley
fare_text: Free.
hours_text: Daily. Eastbound from Grand Central Station every 30 minutes, 6:33 AM-9:33 PM; westbound from 2nd Ave NE and Beach Drive 6:14 AM-9:39 PM (last arrival 10:01 PM).
summary: A free PSTA trolley along Central Avenue between Grand Central Station and the St. Pete Pier (2nd Ave NE and Beach Drive), running every 30 minutes daily.

stops.name: 2nd Ave NE and Beach Drive (St. Pete Pier)

notes: Hours and frequency are read from the posted Sunday-Saturday timetable (eastbound departures at :03 and :33). PSTA's home page listed a Central Avenue Trolley detour for sewer work near Central Avenue and Beach Boulevard on Sep 27, 2026. Verified 2026-09-27: timetable re-read: eastbound columns are Grand Central Station departure and 2nd Ave NE + Beach Drive arrival (6:33 AM departs, 6:55 AM arrives), so departures are every 30 minutes; the '22 minutes' reading was the running time.

name: Clearwater Beach parking
fare_text: City lots $3.50 an hour, no time limit, 6 a.m.-11 p.m. (Clearwater Beach Marina lot $3.50 an hour with a 2-hour limit). On-street $4.00 an hour, 5-hour limit. Pay at pay-by-plate kiosks, with ParkMobile, or by texting CLEARWATER to 727563.
summary: The City of Clearwater runs public parking lots on Clearwater Beach, including the Pier 60 lot (160 S. Gulfview Blvd., 141 spaces) and the Municipal Marina lot (25 Causeway Blvd., 346 spaces); private garages such as the North Beach Parking Plaza (700 spaces), Hyatt, Surf Style and Opal Sol also sell public parking.

stops.name: Pier 60 Parking Lot, 160 S. Gulfview Blvd. (141 spaces)
Municipal Marina Parking Lot, 25 Causeway Blvd. (346 spaces; 2-hour limit)
Parking lot at 4 Rockaway St. (146 spaces)
Parking lot at 420 S. Gulfview Blvd. (65 spaces)
Beach Recreation Center and Library lot, 51 Bay Esplanade (72 spaces)
North Beach Parking Plaza (private), 490 Poinsettia Ave. (700 spaces)

notes: myclearwater.com refuses curl (403); pages were read through WebFetch and the rates cross-checked on two pages. The Municipal Marina lot (zone #9413) has a 2-hour limit; each lot has a zone number on the listing (Pier 60 lot #9414). Read again on Sep 27, 2026 in a headless browser: the city lists ten public lots (Municipal Marina, Pier 60, 420 S. Gulfview, 429 and 461 Mandalay, 4 Rockaway, Avalon-Kendall, Beach Recreation Center, McKay Park, Gateway) and four private garages (North Beach Parking Plaza 700 spaces, Hyatt about 550, Surf Style 300, Opal Sol 290). The Marina lot's 2-hour limit can be extended at $1.00 an hour with a daily code from a boat tour operator or marina restaurant tenant. No public parking north of the Acacia roundabout; no RV parking on Clearwater Beach. Parking System Hotline (727) 562-4094, 8 a.m.-4 p.m. weekdays. The city lists designated rideshare drop-off points (near Baymont Street, San Marco Street, Pier 60 and along Gulfview Blvd). Lot points: census address matches (25 Causeway Blvd., 4 Rockaway St., 51 Bay Esplanade, 490 Poinsettia Ave.); the Pier 60 lot uses the pier-60 place point because the geocoder matched only the street for 160 S. Gulfview Blvd.; 420 S. Gulfview Blvd. likewise matched only the street, so it is not listed.

name: Clearwater Ferry
fare_text: The operator's schedule sheet lists Red Line (Downtown Clearwater-Clearwater Beach Marina) $5.00 regular, $2.50 reduced; Blue Line (Downtown Clearwater-Dunedin) $8.00 regular, $4.00 reduced; 8 and under free. The home page says fares rose by $1 effective Sep 17, 2026, so the sheet may predate the increase.
hours_text: Thursday-Sunday. Red Line 10 a.m.-8:30 p.m.; Blue Line (Dunedin) 10 a.m.-7:00 p.m.
summary: A passenger ferry linking downtown Clearwater (Coachman Park), the Clearwater Beach Marina near Pier 60 and the Dunedin Marina, so you can reach the beach without driving and parking. Reservations are recommended but not required; walk-ons board if there is room, and service can be suspended in bad weather.
notes: Same service as the exp-water experience clearwater-ferry (separate id for the transport record). Stop points are OpenStreetMap ferry-terminal nodes named 'PSTA Clearwater Downtown Ferry Stop', 'PSTA Clearwater Beach Marina Ferry Stop' and 'PSTA Dunedin Marina Ferry Stop'. The schedule PDF shows Red Line departures on the hour from Downtown Clearwater (10:00 AM-8:00 PM) and on the half hour from Clearwater Beach Marina (10:30 AM-7:30 PM), and Blue Line trips every two hours; it carries no date. Weather/text line 727-643-1832. FAQ answers on the site load by script and could not be read. Verified 2026-09-27: home, schedule, getting-there pages and the schedule PDF re-read (headless browser). The Tickets & Fares page shows only the notice 'EFFECTIVE THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 17TH, 2026: PSTA's Clearwater Ferry fare prices will be increased by $1.'; the PDF's fares are undated, so both are given. The City of Clearwater says the Clearwater Beach Marina is being renovated (no transient docks).

name: DASH (Downtown Area Shared Hubs)
fare_text: $2 per person, requested and paid through the DASH Tampa app.
hours_text: Mon-Sat 7 AM-11 PM; Sun 12 PM-9 PM.
summary: An app-hailed, hub-to-hub ride service in downtown Tampa using all-electric vehicles, with more than twenty virtual hubs; each ride costs $2 per person. Wheelchair-accessible rides are provided by partner Wheelchair Transport Service (813-540-3333).
notes: DASH drivers are part of the Partnership's Downtown Ambassadors team. The Partnership says hubs may be adjusted and the app has day-to-day changes. The Tampa Downtown Partnership page links the rider app 'DASH Tampa Microtransit' (package com.ridewithvia.dashtamparider); Visit Tampa Bay's page still links an older app listing. The Downtowner name no longer appears on these Tampa pages; no page read describes a Downtowner service in St. Pete or Clearwater in 2026 (not verified either way). Verified 2026-09-27: DASH page re-read; fare, hours, hubs and accessibility partner match.

name: Downtown Looper
operator: The Looper Group, Inc. (funded in part by PSTA)
fare_text: Free.
hours_text: Mon-Fri 7:00 AM-10:00 PM; Sat-Sun 8:00 AM-10:00 PM; every 15-20 minutes. Not running on Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
summary: A free trolley loop around downtown St. Petersburg every 15-20 minutes, stopping at the Vinoy, St. Pete City Hall, the SouthCore garage, Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital, USF St. Petersburg, the Dali Museum (during museum hours only), the Mahaffey Theater, the James Museum, the Sundial garage and the St. Pete Pier. All trolleys have a wheelchair lift; PSTA's Central Avenue Trolley connects with it on Bayshore Drive near the Pier approach.

stops.name: 6: Florida CraftArt / Central Avenue / Florida Holocaust Museum
14: The Dali Museum (during Dali Museum hours only)
15: Mahaffey Theater / Hilton / Saturday Morning Market
16: Central Avenue / Hampton Inn / The James Museum
19: St. Pete Pier / St. Pete History Museum / Museum of Fine Arts

notes: Verified 2026-09-27. Stops are now taken from the operator's own route map and schedule (Rev 8.1.26, linked from loopertrolley.com), which numbers 18 stops (1-20, no 4 or 10) and gives approximate minutes past the hour; PSTA's route page still lists an older set (BayWalk, Open Air Post Office, 'Cross Bay Ferry at Port St. Pete'), so it is kept only as a source for 'Service funded in part by PSTA but operated by our partners.' The operator's map still labels a Cross Bay Ferry connection 'from Nov to April' and Coast Bike Share stations; both are out of date (see tampa-st-pete-ferry and the bike-share FAQ). Non-service pets ride only in a secured carrier. Contact (727) 821-5166. Stop points are the place records' points (Holocaust Museum, Dali, Mahaffey, James Museum, Pier), census (SouthCore garage entrance) and OpenStreetMap (Sundial garage).

name: Free Beach Ride
operator: Free Beach Ride (Go Green On The Beach LLC)
fare_text: Free; the operator says its drivers welcome tips.
summary: An on-demand, door-to-door shuttle on the southern Gulf beaches, from the south tip of Pass-a-Grille to the northern parts of Madeira Beach. Call 727-776-7553, request a ride online or use its app when you are ready to go; it takes no advance bookings and does not go to the airports.
notes: Added by the verifier, 2026-09-27; found on Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's transportation page and confirmed on the operator's own site (home page title 'Free Community Beach Shuttle, St. Pete Beach, FL'). Fleet: minivans seating 6-7 and open-air vans seating 12-14. Children who need a car seat must bring one. Operating hours are not published on the pages read. Stops are the four beach towns the operator names, not fixed stops.

name: Gateway Expressway (SR 690 and SR 686A)
fare_text: 2-axle car, SunPass / Toll-By-Plate: Gateway Plaza $0.86 / $1.16; Roosevelt Blvd. $0.28 / $0.58 (rates dated May 3, 2024).
summary: A cashless toll road in Pinellas County; St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport's directions page notes that the Gateway Expressway toll road is now open.
notes: The rate sheet heads the page 'Gateway Expressway (SR 690 and SR 686A), Pinellas County' but its table header repeats 'PINELLAS BAYWAY SYSTEM (SR 690 and SR 686A)', an apparent typo on the sheet. The sheet does not describe the road's endpoints, so none are given here. Verified 2026-09-27: rate sheet re-read; rates match; PIE's directions page still says the toll road is now open.

name: Greyhound and FlixBus (Tampa Bus Station)
summary: Greyhound and FlixBus intercity buses use the Tampa Bus Station at HART's Marion Transit Center downtown, with a second stop on the USF campus (Holly Drive at Lot 3D, the Fine Arts Bull Runner stop); both sites list 28 cities reachable directly from Tampa, among them Orlando, Miami, Tallahassee, Atlanta, Fort Myers and Jacksonville.

stops.name: Tampa Bus Station, 1315 N Marion St (Marion Transit Center; Greyhound gates on the North Platform)
University of South Florida, Holly Drive at Lot 3D

notes: Read through WebFetch. Greyhound's page says: 'Greyhound loading gates has relocated From the West Platform to the North Platform.' FlixBus lists the cheapest fares from $6.98 (a promotional 'from' price, not recorded as a fare). The point is HART's GTFS Marion Transit Center stop (the census match for 1315 N Marion St is 27.956948,-82.458706, about 200 m north). HART's schedule book marks Greyhound/FlixBus at the Marion Transit Center. Verified 2026-09-27: Greyhound and FlixBus pages re-read (WebFetch); stops, 28 direct cities and the North Platform notice match.

name: Grouper Airport Express (PIE to Clearwater Beach)
fare_text: One-way: $8 single rider (seniors 65+ $4); $20 total for groups of 3-4; $30 total for groups of 5-8. The airport's own page lists higher fares ($10 single, $30 for four, $40 for five to eight).
hours_text: Every day and time the airport has inbound or outbound flights; book on demand or up to 2 months ahead.
summary: A shared, bookable shuttle between St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport (PIE) and any address on Clearwater Beach, including the Sheraton and Marriott Sand Key resorts; book through grouper.psta.net or the Grouper app. At PIE the pickup is through the west baggage claim exit doors; drivers help with luggage and the service is wheelchair accessible.

stops.name: St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport, west baggage claim exit
Any location on Clearwater Beach (including Sand Key resorts)

notes: Fare conflict: PSTA's Grouper page and the City of Clearwater page say $8/$20/$30; PIE's transportation page says 'Fares begin at $10 for single riders, $30 for group of four, and $40 for groups of five to eight.' The verifier should check which is current. Rides must start and end at PIE or Clearwater Beach; no service within Clearwater Beach or to other Tampa Bay places. Some rides are provided by taxi. Booking needs the web booker or app and a phone that receives texts; no cancellation fees. The PIE point is the OpenStreetMap airfield, not the exit door. Verified 2026-09-27: PSTA and City of Clearwater still say $8/$20/$30; PIE's page still says 'Fares begin at $10'. PSTA operates the service, so its fares lead.

name: Gulf Islands Ferry (Bradenton-Anna Maria Island)
fare_text: Riverwalk-Bridge Street: adult $7 one way, $11 round trip; seniors 60-79, military and children 4-18 $5 one way, $7 round trip; under 3 and 80+ free. Coquina Beach stop: adult $5 one way, $9 round trip. Service fees may apply.
hours_text: Thursday-Sunday (the page's 'Ferry Update' banner; its FAQ still says year-round Wednesday through Sunday, 7:30 a.m.-9:00 p.m.). Bradenton departures 9:30 AM, 10:00 AM, 1:00, 3:00, 4:00 and 7:00 PM; Bridge Street departures 11:30 AM, 1:00, 2:30, 5:30, 6:30 and 8:30 PM. Coquina route: Bridge Street to Coquina 11:00 AM, 12:00, 4:30 and 5:30 PM; Coquina to Bridge Street 11:30 AM, 12:30, 5:00 and 6:00 PM.
summary: A passenger ferry between the Bradenton Riverwalk Pier in downtown Bradenton and the Historic Bridge Street Pier on Anna Maria Island (about 50 minutes), with a 20-minute hop to Coquina Beach; on the island the free trolley connects the beaches. Free parking for the ferry is at the City Centre Parking Facility in downtown Bradenton, a five-minute walk from the pier.

stops.name: Historic Bridge Street Pier, Bradenton Beach

notes: Same service as the exp-water experience gulf-islands-ferry (separate id for the transport record). The source is the Bradenton Area Convention and Visitors Bureau page. It contradicts itself: a banner says the ferry operates 'Thursdays thru Sundays', while the FAQ says 'year-round Wednesday through Sunday from 7:30 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.'; the verifier should confirm. Stop points are OpenStreetMap ferry-terminal nodes (and the Coquina Beach bus stop). Contact 727-200-6487. Verified 2026-09-27: banner re-read: Bradenton departures listed as '930A,10A, 1P, 3P, 4P, 7P' (the earlier record also listed 5:30 PM, which the page does not); the Thursday-Sunday banner is treated as the current days.

name: HART buses
fare_text: Local and Limited Express: $2.00 a trip, capped at $4.00 a day and $65.00 a month when you pay with the Flamingo Fares app or card, a contactless bank card or a phone wallet. Discount fare $1.00 (cap $2.00 a day). 1 Day Family Pass $12.50 (up to 5 people, Flamingo app only). 3-Day Visitor Pass $11.75 (sold only at select HART facilities and hotels). Month Passport $85.00 (HART and PSTA). HARTFlex $1.00. Children 5 and under ride free with a paying adult.
hours_text: Varies by route; routes 10, 30 and 32 serve Tampa International Airport seven days a week.
summary: Hillsborough County's bus system, with local routes, limited-express commuter routes and HARTFlex, meeting at the Marion Transit Center downtown. Routes 10 (Cypress St.) and 30 (Kennedy Blvd./Town 'N Country) link downtown Tampa with the Tampa International Airport Rental Car Center, reached from the terminal by the SkyConnect train.

stops.name: Marion Transit Center, 1211 N Marion St (downtown hub; Greyhound/FlixBus; PSTA 100 and 300)
Tampa International Airport Rental Car Center (routes 10, 30, 32; PSTA 300)

notes: Fare caps apply to Flamingo app/card and to contactless cards or wallets used the same way each time. HART's bus page says routes 10, 30 and 32 can be picked up near the Rental Car Center (take SkyConnect from the Red Baggage Claim); the same page also still describes the In-Towner (Route 96) and names Amalie Arena, so parts of it are dated and its hours for routes 10/30 are not repeated here. The schedule book effective Aug 16, 2026 lists Route 30 (Kennedy Blvd./Town 'N Country, via the airport to the Northwest Transfer Center) and Route 10 (Cypress St.) to the Rental Car Center; Route 32 (Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd.) runs from the Netpark Transfer Center to the airport. The schedules page also lists MetroRapid (Downtown Tampa to UATC/Hidden River Park-n-Ride via Nebraska Ave.). Stop coordinates are from HART's GTFS stops.txt (feed 2608.4). HARTInfo line: 813-254-4278. Verified 2026-09-27: fares page re-read (3-Day Visitor Pass and the under-5 rule added). The bus page's hidden airport block says routes 10, 30 and 32 'can be picked up near the Rental Car Center. Take the Airport's SkyConnect from the Red Baggage Claim to the Rental Car Center'; Route 10 weekday service 5:30 a.m. to midnight, weekends 7 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. (bus page). Schedule book pages 22-24 (Route 10) and 39-41 (Route 30, Downtown Tampa to Tampa Airport to Northwest) confirm the airport routes.

name: Jolley Trolley
fare_text: $2.25 cash fare (exact change; drivers carry no change), reduced $1.10, children 8 and under free; contactless payment and group passes through Flamingo Fares. Guests of the Sandpearl, Opal Sands, Sheraton Sand Key, Marriott Sand Key and TradeWinds ride free with their room card (plus four guests).
hours_text: Daily, 365 days a year. Per PSTA's posted timetables: North Beach Route 9:41 AM-10:01 PM Sunday-Thursday and until about 11:51 PM Friday-Saturday; South Beach Route 9:48 AM-10:10 PM Sunday-Thursday; Coastal Route first northbound trip 8:21 AM from Dunedin (Main St and Pinellas Trail), with the last trips reaching downtown Clearwater at 9:27 PM Sunday-Thursday and 12:27 AM Friday-Saturday.
summary: Trolleys on Clearwater Beach (North Beach and South Beach routes around the beach, Island Estates and Sand Key, as far south as Bay Park) and a Coastal Route from Clearwater Beach and downtown Clearwater to Dunedin, Palm Harbor and the Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks. The fare is $2.25; the trolleys carry two bikes on a front rack and do not go to John's Pass.

stops.name: Clearwater Beach Transit Center (North and South)
Gulf Blvd and Bayside Gardens (Sand Key)
Safford St and Tarpon Ave (Tarpon Springs)

notes: Verified 2026-09-27. The operator's site is clearwaterjolleytrolley.com (linked from the Clearwater Ferry site; jolleytrolley.com does not resolve), read in a headless browser: fares, free-room-card hotels, service animals only, bike rack for two bikes, 'our beach route goes as far south as Sandkey/Bay park' (not John's Pass), routes '7 days a week, 365 days a year'. Coastal Route stops on the operator's list: Beach Transit Center, Clearwater Beach Marina, Park Street (PSTA), Osceola/Cleveland St, Dunedin, Curlew, Ozona (Friday evening-Sunday), Florida Avenue, Alderman, E Tarpon Avenue, Rusty Bellies. Times are from PSTA's timetables (the earlier note placing the 8:21 AM first trip at Clearwater Beach was wrong: it leaves Main St and Pinellas Trail in Dunedin). Clearwater Ferry says the Jolley Trolley added a stop at its downtown Clearwater dock. The Sponge Docks point is the see-pinellas place record; transit center points are OpenStreetMap bus stops.

name: Madeira Beach city parking
fare_text: $4.00 an hour unless otherwise posted (rates effective October 1, 2024). Since mid-April 2026 payment is mobile prepaid through ParkMobile at all municipal paid lots; the Village Blvd lot also has two pay-to-park meters.
summary: The City of Madeira Beach charges $4.00 an hour in its paid lots, paid in the ParkMobile app with the zone number on nearby signs; start the session when you arrive, enter your plate exactly, and park facing the direction of traffic (no back-in parking where posted). Vehicles with a valid disabled plate or certain veterans' plates park free in city-owned lots.
notes: Added by the verifier, 2026-09-27 (the researcher had found no readable official page). Free veterans' plates named by the city: Ex-Prisoner of War, Pearl Harbor Survivor, Medal of Honor, Purple Heart and Disabled Veteran. Parking disputes must be filed online within five business days. Lot names and locations are on the city's parking map (not read), so no points are given. The county's Madeira Beach Access park is a Pinellas County lot (see pinellas-county-beach-park-parking).

name: Rental cars at St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport
hours_text: Alamo/National, Avis and Budget 6:30 AM-11:00 PM daily; Enterprise 6:00 AM-11:00 PM daily; counters stay open 30 minutes after the last arriving flight.
summary: Alamo/National, Avis, Budget and Enterprise have on-site counters at PIE; after hours some serve customers from the rental car parking lot rather than the counter in baggage claim.
notes: The airport advises late-night arrivals to book the latest reservation time available and note the flight number. Point is the OpenStreetMap airfield. Verified 2026-09-27: rental page re-read; companies and hours match.

name: Pinellas Bayway tolls (SR 682 and SR 679)
fare_text: 2-axle car, SunPass / Toll-By-Plate: West Plaza (Bayway II) $0.58 / $1.08; East Plaza (Bayway I) $0.58 / $1.08; South Plaza (Bayway IV, SR 679) $0.28 / $0.81. Commuter pass $50 a year for unlimited 2-axle passage (expires each Sept. 30). Rates effective September 22, 2023.
summary: The Pinellas Bayway system (SR 682 and SR 679) is the tolled causeway route between I-275 in south St. Petersburg and St. Pete Beach, with three cashless plazas: the East Plaza charges westbound, the West Plaza eastbound, and the South Plaza on SR 679 southbound.
notes: Directions per plaza are from the sheet's map (East Plaza: westbound tolls; West Plaza: eastbound; South Plaza: southbound). The map labels St. Pete Beach, South Pasadena and Gulfport around the system; it does not name Tierra Verde or Fort De Soto, so the summary does not either (SR 679 runs south from the Bayway; the verifier may add where it leads from another source). Verified 2026-09-27: rate sheet re-read; rates and the $50 commuter pass (expires Sept. 30) match.

name: Pinellas County beach park parking (Fort De Soto, Sand Key, Fred Howard)
fare_text: Until November 30, 2026: $6 a day at Fort De Soto, Sand Key and Fred Howard parks. From December 1, 2026: beach parking $3.50 an hour, capped at $12 a day, plus tax; boat ramp parking $12 a day. Annual Beach Pass $95 from October 1, 2026 (was $75); 6-month pass $60 (was $45); disabled U.S. veterans free. Pay at pay stations, with the Flowbird or ParkMobile apps, or by text ($0.35 convenience fee for app or text); SunPass is not accepted.
summary: Pinellas County charges for parking at its beach parks; an annual beach pass is valid at Fort De Soto Park, Sand Key Park and Fred Howard Park Beach. The county's rates change on October 1, 2026 (passes) and December 1, 2026 (hourly and daily parking), and Fort De Soto Park is cashless: pay at a machine or by app, not at the entry booth.
notes: Verified 2026-09-27. The county's beaches page says 'A $6 per day parking fee applies to Fort De Soto, Sand Key and Fred Howard parks'; the annual-permits page (updated Sep 25, 2026) gives the new pass prices from Oct 1, 2026 and the hourly/daily rates from Dec 1, 2026. The FAQ: Fort De Soto is cashless (the entry booth no longer takes payment) and SunPass is not accepted for parking. Passes: explore.pinellas.gov, 727-582-2100 (Option 2), or 12520 Ulmerton Road, Largo. Park points are the outdoors slice's place records.

name: Pirate Water Taxi
fare_text: All-Day Pass: adult $34, child (ages 2-12) $24; Annual Membership $199.95. Cashless on the boat; tickets online or at the booth at Stop 7.
hours_text: Mon-Thu 11:30 AM-6:30 PM; Fri-Sun 11:30 AM-9:30 PM. On weekdays boats leave Stop 7 toward Stop 16 at 11:30 AM, 1:00, 2:30, 4:00 and 5:30 PM; departures are more frequent Friday-Sunday.
summary: A hop-on, hop-off water taxi on the Hillsborough River and the Channel District waterfront with 10 numbered stops from the Florida Aquarium to Armature Works; an all-day pass covers unlimited rides. Boats are covered and wheelchair accessible, though not every dock is; bikes and luggage are not allowed on board, and service stops for lightning, heavy rain and high winds.

stops.name: Stop 7: Convention Center / Marriott Water Street (home dock and ticket booth, 333 S Franklin St)
Stop 15: Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park
Stop 3: Benchmark International Arena / Tampa History Center
Stop 2: Sparkman Wharf / Yacht StarShip / Craft
Stop 1: Florida Aquarium / American Victory Ship

notes: Same service as the exp-water experience pirate-water-taxi (kept under a separate id here because this is the transport record). Stops are listed in the order the schedule serves them (7, 8, 11, 12, 15, 16, then 4, 3, 2, 1 and back to 7). Stop coordinates are the named landmark (the place records' points: census or OpenStreetMap), not the dock itself; Stop 11 (Arabelle Riverwalk) and Stop 4 (Harbour Island) have no point because no source placed the dock. The map page says route schedule and stop availability may be affected by low or high tides. FAQ: no reservations needed (first-come, first-served); children 13 and under must ride with someone 14 or older; the boats do not go to St. Pete; the zoo route was discontinued in 2017; parking is not included (the FAQ suggests the Tampa Convention Center, Pam Iorio and Fort Brooke garages). Verified 2026-09-27: schedule, rates ($34/$24, annual $199.95), FAQ and map pages re-read; all match. Stop 1's point was corrected to the florida-aquarium place point (the earlier point sat about 220 m west, at Sparkman Wharf). The site also advertises a Rain Day Guarantee (if rain stops service for more than 90 minutes, you may return the next day) and live-tracking links for a 'River Route' and an 'Island Loop'.

name: Port Tampa Bay cruise terminals
fare_text: Cruise parking is prepaid online through the port's parking link (rates not shown on the pages read); valet upgrade $20.
summary: Tampa homeports eight ships from five cruise lines (Carnival, Royal Caribbean, Celebrity, Norwegian and Margaritaville at Sea) at three terminals along Channelside Drive in the Channel District; the port's garage is across the street from Terminal 3. The terminals have no luggage storage for early arrivals; the port says the Florida Aquarium next to Terminal 2 stores luggage free with a discounted admission ticket.

stops.name: Cruise Terminal 3, 815 Channelside Drive (parking garage across the street)

notes: Terminal points are OpenStreetMap buildings (Photon); the garage point is a census address match. Drop-off and valet follow the BLUE ROUTE, self-parking the RED ROUTE (terminal guide). Disabled-veteran plates and certain modified vehicles park free under Florida law at 810 Channelside Drive and 1331 McKay Street when a ship is in port. The port says Tampa International Airport is a 15-minute drive from the Channelside District. The TECO Line Streetcar's Port Tampa Bay Station (#5) and York Street Station (#6) are nearby. Visit Tampa Bay's page names Holland America instead of Celebrity and Margaritaville at Sea; the port's own list is used. Verified 2026-09-27: overview, terminal guide and parking pages re-read; lines, terminals, garage, $20 valet upgrade and luggage rule match. The prepaid parking vendor (tickets.completeticketsolutions.com) shows a Cloudflare check to every reader, so cruise parking rates remain unknown.

name: 727 Airport Express (downtown St. Petersburg to Tampa International Airport)
hours_text: Seven days a week, 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM (PSTA).
season_text: Launching October 4, 2026, per PSTA; not yet running on Sep 27, 2026. Fare, frequency and stop names were not published on the pages read.
summary: A new PSTA premium express bus between nine stops in downtown St. Petersburg and Tampa International Airport, running over the Howard Frankland Bridge express lanes on I-275. PSTA says it will run daily from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. on hybrid buses with luggage racks.

stops.name: Downtown St. Petersburg (nine stops; names not yet published)

notes: Added by the verifier, 2026-09-27. Found through Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's transportation page ('Tampa Airport Express (Route 727)'), then confirmed on PSTA's own pages: the service page ('Launching October 4th!', '7 days a week, 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM', 'Hybrid buses with spacious luggage racks', connections with the SunRunner), the July 27, 2026 release (nine stops in downtown St. Petersburg, then direct to TPA via the Howard Frankland Bridge Express Lanes; vehicles with luggage racks) and the Sep 24, 2026 budget release ('set to launch October 4, 2026'). name: PSTA buses
fare_text: $2.25 a ride; with Flamingo Fares or tap-to-pay the most you pay is $5 a day and $85 a calendar month. Reduced fare $1.10 (cap $2.50 a day). Cash (exact change, no pennies) is accepted on all routes except the SunRunner, without fare caps. Children 8 and under ride free. 1 Day Flamingo Fares Group Pass $5 for up to 4 people.
summary: Pinellas County's transit agency: fixed-route buses, the SunRunner rapid bus, the Suncoast Beach Trolley along the Gulf beaches, and express routes 100 and 300 to downtown Tampa. Tap a contactless card (not American Express), Apple Pay, Google Pay or the Flamingo Fares app to get the daily and monthly fare caps.
notes: PSTA's own description (press releases, 2026): 41 fixed-route bus routes, two express routes to downtown Tampa, the Suncoast Beach Trolley, the Jolley Trolley and the Looper, and 10.7 million rides a year. US military veterans ride free with a PSTA veterans pass (fares page). Customer information: (727) 540-1900 (per the Looper site). The PSTA site listed many route detours on Sep 27, 2026; they are not recorded. Verified 2026-09-27: fares page re-read; all amounts match.

name: PSTA Route 100 Express (St. Petersburg to Tampa)
fare_text: Regular PSTA fare ($2.25).
hours_text: Monday-Friday only. First eastbound trip leaves 2nd Ave NE and Beach Drive at 4:47 AM; last westbound trip leaves the Marion Transit Center at 7:18 PM.
summary: A weekday express bus between the St. Pete Pier area (2nd Ave NE and Beach Drive) and the Marion Transit Center in downtown Tampa, stopping at Gateway Mall and Britton Plaza.

stops.name: 2nd Ave NE and Beach Drive (St. Pete Pier)

notes: Times read from the posted Monday-Friday timetable (eastbound and westbound). The route page does not state a separate express fare; the fares page gives $2.25 for PSTA rides. A detour at Central Avenue and Bayshore Blvd (sewer work) was posted on Sep 27, 2026. Verified 2026-09-27: full westbound timetable re-read: 12 trips, 6:10 AM-7:18 PM from the Marion Transit Parking Lot; eastbound 4:47 AM first trip, last 5:47 PM from 2nd Ave NE and Beach Drive.

name: PSTA Route 300 Express (Largo to Tampa Airport and downtown Tampa)
fare_text: Regular PSTA fare ($2.25).
summary: A weekday limited-stop express from the Ulmerton Park and Ride in Largo via the Tampa International Airport Rental Car Center to the Marion Transit Center in downtown Tampa.

The Ulmerton Park and Ride point is the OpenStreetMap bus stop 'Ulmerton Park North Ride Lot'; the airport and Marion points are HART's GTFS stops. The PSTA 34th St layby stop has no point. 'Via Feather Sound' was removed from the summary and the area guess on the 34th St layby stop was dropped: the route page does not say where the layby is.

name: RedCoach (Tampa stop at USF)
summary: RedCoach intercity buses stop on the USF campus (3801 USF Holly Drive) and run from Tampa to Miami, Fort Lauderdale, Fort Myers, Naples, Gainesville, Ocala and Tallahassee (FSU).
notes: Read through WebFetch. Verified 2026-09-27: stop address and destinations re-read. A one-day notice for Saturday 09/26 (campus closed for games; buses at a downtown stop at 329 Marriott Dr) is past and appears to concern the FSU stop, so it is not recorded. Route prices shown on the home page are promotional 'from' prices and are not recorded. No coordinates: the geocoder matched only the street (USF Holly Drive), not the stop.

name: Tolls in a rental car
summary: Most rental companies include tolls through their own programs (plate photos or transponders), each with its own fees, so read the rental agreement. If you have a SunPass PRO or other portable transponder, add the rental car's plate and dates to your SunPass account (online or 1-888-865-5352) and remove the transponder when you return the car.
notes: The page says Toll-By-Plate is not available for customers in rental cars because invoices go to the registered owner. SunPass Customer Service hours given: 7:00 A.M.-7:00 P.M. Monday-Friday, closed weekends. The page calls the movable transponder 'SunPass Portable'; the SunPass page names the SunPass PRO as the movable one. Verified 2026-09-27: page re-read; matches.

name: Sarasota Bradenton International Airport
summary: The airport serving Sarasota and Bradenton, run by the Sarasota Manatee Airport Authority; Uber and Lyft pick up at the far west end of the ticket wing in the Ground Transportation area, taxis must be called ahead, and Sarasota County Breeze Transit and Manatee County Area Transit (MCAT) buses stop there.
notes: Read through WebFetch (flysrq.com blocks curl with a Cloudflare check), so wording was checked twice but not against raw HTML. Airlines named on the home page: Southwest, Allegiant, American, United, Breeze, Avelo, Frontier, Sun Country. Point is the OpenStreetMap airfield (it lists the street as 6000 Airport Circle). Verified 2026-09-27 (WebFetch; flysrq.com shows a Cloudflare check to curl and to a headless browser): the home page names the Sarasota Manatee Airport Authority (SMAA) as the airport's operator; ten hotels are permitted to pick up guests in the Ground Transportation area.

name: Lee Roy Selmon Expressway
fare_text: 2-axle car, SunPass / Toll-By-Plate (rates effective July 1, 2026): Reversible Express Lanes $2.18 / $2.54; East Main Plaza (78th St.) $2.18 / $2.54; West Main Plaza (Hyde Park) $1.44 / $1.80; 50th St., Willow Ave. and Selmon West Extension $1.07 / $1.43; 22nd St. and Plant Ave. $0.75 / $1.11. The I-4 Connector to the Selmon adds $0.57-$1.13 (SunPass). Toll-By-Plate tolls are subject to an administration fee.
summary: A 17-mile all-electronic toll road that, with the Selmon West Extension, runs from the south end of the Gandy Bridge through downtown Tampa to I-75 in Brandon without a stoplight. Its upper deck of Reversible Express Lanes carries westbound traffic in the morning and eastbound traffic in the evening and on weekends.
notes: Rates are THEA's toll table (2-axle). The I-4 Connector (FDOT, rates effective July 1, 2023) links I-4 with the Selmon and the port: SunPass $1.13 ('S' move, to/from the west on the Selmon) or $0.57 ('Z' move, to/from the east); Toll-By-Plate $1.41 / $0.84. The Pirate Water Taxi's directions page routes drivers from the Selmon (exit 7, Brorein St.) to downtown. Verified 2026-09-27: THEA toll calculator re-read ('New Rates Effective July 1st, 2026'); 50th Street added.

name: St. Pete Beach public beach parking
fare_text: $5.00 an hour Monday-Thursday and $6.00 an hour Friday-Sunday, plus a $1.00-an-hour seasonal surcharge February 1-April 30; boat trailers $25 a day at the boat ramps. Pay by card at pay stations (no cash or coins), with the ParkMobile app, or by text (text 'Park' to 77223).
summary: St. Pete Beach lists its public beach parking: Pass-a-Grille Beach (541 spaces on Gulf Way and 186 on Pass-a-Grille Way), Upham Beach (183 spaces at Beach Plaza and 67th Ave, plus smaller lots on Sunset Way and 75th Ave) and the county Beach Access Park at 4700 Gulf Blvd (223 spaces).

stops.name: Pass-a-Grille Beach: Gulf Way (541 spaces) and Pass-a-Grille Way (186 spaces)
Upham Beach, 6850 Beach Plaza (Beach Plaza and 67th Ave: 183 spaces)
County Beach Access Park, 4700 Gulf Blvd (223 spaces)

notes: Verified 2026-09-27: locations page and the 'How to Pay for Parking' page read in a headless browser (the site resets curl). Park only in pay-by-plate spaces; where signs require a permit (B, 2R-U, 3R-B, 3R-D, 4R) public parking is not allowed. Shared parking 0.5 mile from Upham Beach: Bank of America lot, 6800 Gulf Blvd (public 6 pm-6 am weekdays, 8 am-6 am weekends) and Fit4Life lot, 575 75th Ave (noon-6 am daily). Points are census address matches.

name: St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport
fare_text: Parking (new rates effective 10/1/26): Long Term $2.00 first hour, $1.00 each additional 20 minutes, $16.00 daily maximum; Short Term $25.00 daily maximum; Economy $12.00 per day.
summary: The airport on Roosevelt Blvd (SR 686), 4 miles north of St. Petersburg, served by Allegiant and Sun Country (domestic) and BermudAir (international), with nonstops to more than 60 cities. Rideshare pickup is in front of the terminal at Arrivals; taxis and shuttles wait in the Ground Transportation lot outside baggage claim; PSTA's Grouper runs to Clearwater Beach.
notes: Airlines page (Sep 27, 2026): Allegiant and Sun Country (domestic), BermudAir (Anguilla, Turks and Caicos, Belize), plus casino charters. Parking is first-come, first-served (no reservations); Economy lots Key Lime (across Roosevelt Blvd on 46th Street) and Strawberry (Fairchild Drive, opens as needed) with free shuttles. On-site rental cars: Alamo/National, Avis, Budget, Enterprise (counters in baggage claim). Taxi: United Taxi and Yellow Cab (727) 777-7777. The directions page says the Gateway Expressway toll road is now open. Point is the OpenStreetMap airfield (the census geocoder returned the same feature). The airport's owner/operator is not named on the pages read, so operator is null. Verified 2026-09-27: transportation, parking (new rates effective 10/1/26), directions, airlines and rental pages re-read; all match.

name: St. Petersburg downtown parking
fare_text: Meters $1 to $1.50 an hour (card, coins or ParkMobile). SouthCore Garage $2 an hour, $16 a day. Al Lang surface lot $5 a day. 800 1st Ave S lot $3 a day. Event rates vary.
summary: St. Petersburg has metered, time-limited and free on-street parking plus city garages and lots downtown; pay meters by card, coins or the ParkMobile app, and read the meter for enforcement hours. The SouthCore Garage (entrance at 101 1st Ave. S) has more than 1,124 spaces, EV charging on level 7 and a 6 ft 10 in height limit.

stops.name: SouthCore Parking Garage, entrance at 101 1st Ave. S
Al Lang / Progress Energy Park surface lot, 1st Ave. S between 1st St. and Bayshore Dr. (328 spaces, open 24/7)
Lot 2, 6th St. N between 1st Ave. N and Mirror Lake Dr (64 spaces)

notes: ParkMobile fee per the city: $0.35 per transaction (or $1.75 a month plus $0.25 per transaction). SouthCore: floors 3, 4, 7 and 8 for visitors; next-day rate begins at 5 a.m.; $5 flat Saturday mornings October to May; lost ticket $25; operator SP Plus 727-896-2256. For Pier parking the city points to the St. Pete Pier website (not read). The same city page says PSTA's Central Avenue Trolley runs 'to Pass-A-Grille on St. Pete Beach'; PSTA's current route page shows it running only between Grand Central Station and the Pier, so that line is treated as out of date. SouthCore and 800 1st Ave S points are census address matches; the Al Lang lot uses the al-lang-stadium place. Verified 2026-09-27: city page re-read; rates, spaces and SouthCore details match.

name: St. Pete bike share (Lime e-bikes)
operator: Lime, in partnership with the City of St. Petersburg
summary: St. Petersburg's downtown bike share uses Lime Gen4 e-bikes rented in the Lime app; you must be 18 or older, may not ride on sidewalks, and must end the ride at a designated bike-share hub.
notes: Prices are set in the Lime app and not stated on the city page; the city's scooter page lists a Lime 'St. Pete Pass' ($40.99 for 250 minutes plus free unlocks) for Lime vehicles. Lime Access offers discounts to eligible riders. Verified 2026-09-27: city page re-read; rules match.

name: St. Pete Pier parking
fare_text: Dolphin and Pelican lots, weekdays (Monday 12:00 AM-Friday 5:00 PM): $2 an hour for the first 4 hours, $3 the 5th hour, $4 the 6th, 6-hour maximum ($15). Weekends (Friday 5:00 PM-Sunday 11:59 PM): $2.50 an hour for 4 hours, then $3.50 and $4.50, 6-hour maximum ($18). On-street meters: $2.50 an hour for 3 hours, $5 the 4th hour, 4-hour maximum ($12.50), enforced daily 9:00 AM-10:00 PM. Pay by card, cash at the pay machines, or ParkMobile.
summary: The Pier has more than 500 on-site parking spaces in its Dolphin and Pelican lots, with six EV charging stations. Demand peaks Friday 4-9 PM and Saturday 1-8 PM, when the Pier suggests overflow parking in the Sundial garage or the Al Lang lot, both within walking distance; vehicles that need more than one space cannot park on the Pier.

stops.name: Dolphin and Pelican lots (on the Pier)
Sundial Parking Garage (overflow; enter on 2nd St. N just south of 2nd Ave. N)
Al Lang Parking Lot (overflow; enter on 1st Ave. S between Beach Dr. and Bayshore Dr.)

notes: Added by the verifier, 2026-09-27 (the City of St. Petersburg's parking page points to the Pier's site for Pier parking). Pier hours: opens 30 minutes before sunrise, closes 11:00 PM. Oversized vehicles up to 30 ft may load and unload in the Pelican lot bus lane; questions 727-244-6189. The Pier page says the closest SunRunner stop is 5th Street N (Stop #1111). Points: the st-pete-pier place (Dolphin/Pelican lots are on the Pier), OpenStreetMap (Sundial garage) and the al-lang-stadium place.

name: Shared e-scooters (St. Petersburg)
operator: Spin and Lime, under the City of St. Petersburg program
fare_text: Spin: $1 to unlock + $0.42/min (St. Pete resident rate $1 + $0.34/min; or $1.50 per mile + $1 unlock). Lime: per-minute pricing that varies by demand; St. Pete Pass $40.99 for 250 minutes with free unlocks.
summary: Spin and Lime rent standing and seated e-scooters in St. Petersburg through their apps. The city's rules: no sidewalk riding, one rider per scooter, riders 18 and older with a license or photo ID, ride in bike lanes or on streets of 30 mph or less, not along the waterfront trails or on the Pier (corrals are at the base of the Pier), and park in designated corrals.
notes: The city's Transportation Options page names only Spin for e-scooters, while the scooter page lists both Spin and Lime as vendors. The scooter page also says 'Wear a helmet' in its rules list. Spin support 1-888-249-9698. Verified 2026-09-27: city page re-read; prices and rules match.

name: Suncoast Beach Trolley
fare_text: PSTA fares apply: $2.25 a ride; $5 daily cap with Flamingo Fares or tap-to-pay.
hours_text: Daily including holidays. Northbound trips leave 75th Ave and Gulf Blvd from 5:12 AM, generally every 30 minutes; the southbound timetable runs until about 10:20 PM.
summary: A PSTA trolley route along Gulf Boulevard linking the Gulf beach towns from St. Pete Beach (75th Ave) through Treasure Island, John's Pass, Madeira Beach, the Redingtons, Indian Shores, Indian Rocks Beach and Sand Key to Clearwater Beach and the Park Street Terminal in downtown Clearwater.

stops.name: 75th Ave and Gulf Blvd (St. Pete Beach)
Park Street Terminal (Garden Ave and Park St, downtown Clearwater)

notes: The route page lists: St. Pete Beach, 75th Ave and Gulf Blvd, Treasure Island, John's Pass Village, Madeira Beach, Redington Beach, North Redington Beach, Redington Shores, Park Blvd Boat Ramp, Indian Shores, Indian Rocks Beach, Bay Park, Clearwater Sailing Center, Sand Key, Pier 60, Clearwater Beach, Mandalay Park, Island Estates (intermittent) and Park Street Terminal. The route page does not state a fare; Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's transportation page gives '$2.25 per ride', matching PSTA's fares page. Transit-center points are OpenStreetMap bus stops. Verified 2026-09-27: route page re-read: stops list, first northbound 5:12 AM from 75th Ave and Gulf Blvd, last southbound arrival 10:20 PM at Gulf Blvd and Marina Del Rey Ct, daily including holidays.

name: SunPass
operator: Florida Department of Transportation (Florida's Turnpike Enterprise)
fare_text: Transponders: SunPass Mini $4.99 + tax (sticks to the windshield; Florida, Georgia, Kansas, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Texas); SunPass PRO $14.95 + tax (movable between cars; also works where E-ZPass is accepted). A prepaid balance is required.
summary: Florida's prepaid electronic toll account; SunPass users pay the lowest toll rate and, per Florida's Turnpike, save an average of 25% compared with Toll-By-Plate. Tampa Bay's toll roads are cashless, and they also accept E-ZPass, E-PASS, Peach Pass, NC Quick Pass and several other transponders.
notes: Accepted in electronic toll lanes (Turnpike's list): SunPass, E-PASS, E-ZPass, LeeWay, ExpressToll, Peach Pass and NC Quick Pass, PIKEPASS, K-TAG, EZTAG and TollTag. Tampa-area electronic toll locations on the Turnpike's list: Veterans Expressway, Suncoast Parkway, I-4 Connector, Selmon Expressway (THEA) and Sunshine Skyway Bridge. The Toll Relief Program ran April 1, 2024-March 31, 2025 and has ended. sunpass.com itself is a script-driven site that returned no readable text. Verified 2026-09-27: SunPass page re-read; prices, states and the ended Toll Relief Program match. SunPass customer service per this page: Monday-Friday 7:00 AM-7:00 PM, Saturday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM (the rental-vehicles page says closed weekends).

name: SunRunner
fare_text: Same as regular PSTA service: $2.25 a ride (reduced fares available). Cashless: tap a contactless Visa, Mastercard or Discover card, phone or watch, or use Flamingo Fares; American Express and cash are not accepted.
hours_text: Seven days a week, 6 AM to midnight. Every 15 minutes until 8 PM, then every 30 minutes until midnight; every 15 minutes until midnight on Fridays and Saturdays (SunRunner After Dark).
summary: Tampa Bay's first bus rapid transit line, a 10-mile, 16-stop route with dedicated bus lanes between downtown St. Petersburg and St. Pete Beach via the Grand Central and EDGE districts and South Pasadena; PSTA says the trip takes about 35 minutes. Buses have level boarding, three interior bike racks, free Wi-Fi and charging at every seat.
notes: PSTA lists destinations served: downtown St. Petersburg, USF St. Pete, Tropicana Field, TradeWinds Island Resort, the Grand Central and EDGE business districts, Bayfront, Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital, South Pasadena and St. Pete Beach. The page says 31 stations (both directions) and a 10-mile, 16-stop line; station names and points were not published in the pages read, so stops are the three areas only. Rental bikes and scooters and tandem bikes are not allowed on board; small pets in carriers are. The page links bike share at gohopr.com/coast, which now says Coast Bike Share has closed (see the bike-share records). Verified 2026-09-27: service page re-read; hours, frequency, SunRunner After Dark, 10-mile 16-stop line, 35 minutes, cashless, no American Express all match.

name: Sunshine Skyway Bridge toll (I-275)
fare_text: 2-axle car: $1.16 with SunPass, $1.62 by Toll-By-Plate, at each of the North Plaza and the South Plaza (rates effective April 12, 2026). Cash is not accepted.
summary: The I-275 bridge across the mouth of Tampa Bay between St. Petersburg and Manatee County (Palmetto and Bradenton) is a cashless toll: pay with SunPass or another accepted transponder, or be billed by Toll-By-Plate.
notes: The rate sheet lists the same rates at '15 - NORTH PLAZA' and '6 - SOUTH PLAZA' without saying which direction each charges, so we do not say whether a one-way crossing passes one or both plazas. The Turnpike's electronic toll collection page lists the Sunshine Skyway Bridge among Tampa-area locations where cash is not accepted. Verified 2026-09-27: rate sheet re-read; $1.16 / $1.62 at both plazas, effective April 12, 2026.

name: City of Tampa parking (downtown, Ybor City and neighborhoods)
fare_text: Garages: $3 an hour, $18 daily max (Ft. Brooke, W.F. Poe, Pam Iorio, Convention Center); $2 an hour, $14 daily max (Twiggs, Centro Ybor, Palm Ave.). On-street: downtown $4 first hour, $3 each hour after; Hyde Park, Ybor, Armature Works, Channel District, Davis Islands and Grand Central $3 first hour, $2 after. Ybor lots: first two hours free, then $2 an hour, $14 max ($10 flat Fri-Sat 8 p.m.-3 a.m.). Florida Aquarium lot $5 an hour, no daily max.
summary: The City of Tampa runs garages and lots downtown and in Ybor City plus metered on-street parking; pay at pay stations or with the Passport, PayByPhone, ParkMobile or Flowbird apps using the zone number on the sign (a convenience fee applies). Special-event rates apply until 6 a.m., and next-day charges start at 6 a.m.
notes: Rates page updated 10/13/2025; the city may charge a flat rate at its discretion. The Tampa Downtown Partnership says downtown has more than 32,000 parking spaces. Garage addresses were not on the pages read; garage points are OpenStreetMap parking features matched by name (Fort Brooke, William F. Poe, Pam Iorio, Twiggs Street at 901 E Twiggs St, Centro Ybor, Convention Center). The Palm Ave. garage has no point (the name search matched a garage in Sarasota). Ben T. Davis Beach lot: $2 an hour, $14 max. Verified 2026-09-27: rates page (updated 10/13/2025) re-read; all rates match. The Palm Ave. garage's area was dropped: the page does not say where it is.

name: Tampa International Airport
summary: Tampa's airport, about five miles west of downtown Tampa, has a central main terminal linked by automated shuttles to Airsides A, C, E and F. The SkyConnect train runs from the main terminal to the Economy Parking garage and the Rental Car Center, where the HART and PSTA bus stop is; Yellow Cab taxis wait outside baggage claim and charge a $40 flat rate to downtown Tampa and the cruise terminal.

stops.name: Main (Landside) Terminal - SkyConnect Passenger Terminal Station
SkyConnect Rental Car Center Station (HART and PSTA bus platform)

address: 4100 George J. Bean Parkway, Tampa, FL 33607
notes: Verified 2026-09-27 against the airport's own pages, read in a headless browser (curl and WebFetch get a Cloudflare 403). Ground Transportation page: rental cars at the Rental Car Center via SkyConnect; remote bag check for most domestic passengers 5:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; Yellow Cab at the Ground Transportation Areas Red 1 and Blue 2 on the baggage claim level, $3.50 for the first 1/5 mile plus $2.85 a mile, $22 minimum from the airport, $40 flat rate to downtown Tampa and the cruise terminal; HART and PSTA bus stop at the Rental Car Center; Lyft, Uber and Wridz pick up at Red Express Curbside, Blue Express Curbside or the SkyCenter One remote curbside with a $5.00 fee; hotel and charter buses in the four ground transportation quad lots (Blue 1, Blue 2, Red 1, Red 2) on level 1. Directions page: 'located just five miles west of downtown Tampa' (Wikipedia says six); address 4100 George J. Bean Parkway. Airlines page lists airlines at Airsides A, C, E and F. The airside shuttles (automated people movers) and Airside D (16 gates, groundbreaking December 2024, scheduled to open in 2028) are from Wikipedia. On Sep 27, 2026 the site carried a traffic alert: Red Departures lanes closed for resurfacing, Red Side drop-offs detoured to the Red Express departures lanes. Airport point is the OpenStreetMap aerodrome; station points are HART's GTFS. 2025 passengers: 24,811,253 (airport activity report, see facts).

name: Shared e-scooters and e-bikes (Tampa)
operator: Lime and Spin, under the City of Tampa Shared Micromobility Program
summary: Lime and Spin rent e-scooters and e-bikes across the City of Tampa through their apps; riders must be 16 or older with a valid driver's license or permit, and helmets are encouraged but not required. The city bars them from the Tampa Riverwalk, Bayshore Boulevard and 7th Avenue in Ybor City, and asks riders to park upright in designated corrals.
notes: City page (updated 05/07/2025) names two vendors, Lime (www.li.me, 1-888-LIME-345) and Spin (www.spin.app, 1-888-262-5189); vehicles travel up to about 15 mph and 15-20 miles per charge. Fares are set in the vendors' apps and are not on the city page. Visit Tampa Bay's transportation page also names Bird; the city page does not, so Bird is not listed here. The page's '7th Avenue' is read as Ybor City's 7th Avenue (the page does not say which). Verified 2026-09-27: city page (updated 05/07/2025) re-read; rules match.

name: Tampa Bay Ferry (St. Petersburg-Tampa)
season_text: Not running as of Sep 27, 2026. PSTA's Sep 24, 2026 budget release says the service 'is scheduled to launch later this year'; no start date, docks, fares or schedule are published.
summary: There is no passenger ferry across the bay between downtown St. Petersburg and Tampa right now: PSTA is preparing a new Tampa Bay Ferry service to replace the former Cross-Bay Ferry, with two vessels (Bay Breeze and Clipper) being refurbished in Tarpon Springs and a permanent dock planned in downtown St. Petersburg.
notes: PSTA press releases of June 22, Sep 4 and Sep 8, 2026. The June release says no launch date is confirmed and calls the old service 'the previous Cross-Bay Ferry model'; the Sep 4 release says PSTA will announce a start date once refurbishment is nearing completion. crossbayferry.com showed only a parked/consent page on Sep 27, 2026. PSTA also received a $16.5 million FTA grant to buy a new vessel. Same subject as the exp-water experience tampa-bay-ferry (opening-soon). No docks, fares or schedule are published, so none are recorded; the Looper and PSTA pages still name a 'Cross Bay Ferry at Port St. Pete' stop. Verified 2026-09-27: PSTA's Sep 24, 2026 release: 'The Tampa Bay Ferry service from downtown St. Petersburg to downtown Tampa is scheduled to launch later this year.' The St. Pete Pier's page says the ferry 'is currently not running but is anticipated to start again in Fall of 2026' and still links thecrossbayferry.com. Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's transportation page still describes a November-May Cross Bay Ferry (out of date).

name: TECO Line Streetcar
operator: HART, under contract to Tampa Historic Streetcar, Inc.
fare_text: Free: all rides are fare free.
hours_text: Every 15 minutes. Mon-Thu 7:00 AM-11:00 PM; Fri 7:00 AM-2:00 AM; Sat 9:00 AM-2:00 AM; Sun 8:30 AM-11:00 PM. Runs until midnight Sun-Thu when there is a Lightning game or evening event at Benchmark International Arena.
summary: A free electric heritage streetcar on a 2.7-mile line with 11 covered, wheelchair-accessible stations linking downtown Tampa, the Channel District and Ybor City; an end-to-end trip takes about 25 minutes. Pull the overhead cord to request your stop; bikes are not allowed on board.

Dick Greco Plaza Station (#10), Franklin St & Old Water St
HSBC Station (#9), Morgan St & Old Water St

The Florida Aquarium Station (#7), Cumberland Ave & Channelside Dr

Port Tampa Bay Station (#5), McKay St & Channelside Dr

notes: Stop coordinates are HART's own (GTFS feed version 2608.4, stops.txt, route 800), i.e. operator-published. Service change effective June 22, 2025: a consistent 15-minute frequency 7 days a week (12-minute peak service discontinued). Pets: service dogs; non-service dogs in small carriers. Extension: the City of Tampa's InVision: Tampa Streetcar page describes a preferred alternative with modern vehicles and a 1.3-mile extension from the western end through downtown to Tampa Heights, in project development; the page gives no construction or opening date, so nothing is scheduled as far as the pages read show. A rider alert on the home page (Sant' Yago Knight Parade) is event-specific and not recorded. The How to Ride page still lists Coast Bike Share among connections; see the bike-share record. Verified 2026-09-27: operator home, How to Ride and About pages re-read; fare, hours, stations, 25-minute running time, extended arena-night service and rules all match; the city's InVision page (updated 06/04/2026) still gives no construction date.

name: Toll-By-Plate
operator: Florida Department of Transportation (Florida's Turnpike Enterprise)
fare_text: Higher per-toll rates than SunPass, plus a $2.50 administrative fee on each invoice (tolls billed over a 30-day period).
summary: If a car without a SunPass or other accepted transponder goes through a cashless toll point, a camera photographs the plate and a toll invoice covering 30 days of tolls plus a $2.50 administrative fee is mailed to the registered owner. Toll-By-Plate cannot be used in Florida's managed (express) lanes and is not available to renters: tolls in a rental car go to the rental company.
notes: Verified 2026-09-27: page re-read; $2.50 fee, 30-day invoice and managed-lane rule match; the rental-car rule is on the rental-vehicles page.

name: Parking at Tampa International Airport
fare_text: Short Term Garage: first hour free, $8 for 1-2 hours and $8 each additional hour, $32 maximum per 24 hours. Long Term Garage: first hour free, $8 for 1-2 hours and $8 each additional hour, $26 maximum per 24 hours. Economy Parking: first hour free, $5 each additional hour, $22 maximum per 24 hours. Maximums include tax; 45-day limit. Cell Phone Waiting Lot free. Booking online may cost less.
summary: TPA has three covered garages: Short Term on levels 4-9 above the main terminal, Long Term next to it (moving walkway on level 4), and Economy south of the terminal, linked by the SkyConnect train; the Cell Phone Waiting Lot is free. The airport takes cash, major cards, SunPass Plus, Apple Pay and Google Pay, and offers free EV charging at most of its parking facilities.

stops.name: Short Term Garage (levels 4-9 above the main terminal)
Long Term Garage (next to the main terminal)
Economy Parking garage (SkyConnect Economy Parking station)

address: 4100 George J. Bean Parkway, Tampa, FL 33607
notes: Added by the verifier, 2026-09-27, from the airport's parking page read in a headless browser (curl and WebFetch get a Cloudflare 403). Vehicle clearance: Short Term 6 ft 8 in, Long Term 7 ft 10 in, Economy levels 2-6 8 ft (level 1 and surface lot 13 ft). The page showed a visitor notice about lane closures while new parking equipment is installed at the garage entrances and exits. Peer-to-peer car sharing is only allowed in the Economy garage (ground transportation page). The record point is the airport; the Economy point is the SkyConnect station from HART's GTFS.

name: Tampa International Airport Rental Car Center
summary: TPA's on-airport rental car companies (Alamo, Avis, Budget, Dollar, Enterprise, Hertz, National, Thrifty, Ace, American, Fox, Payless, Sixt and Zipcar) are in the Rental Car Center, reached from the main terminal by the SkyConnect train. Most domestic passengers can check bags there from 5:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (at least 90 minutes before departure), and the HART and PSTA bus stop is at its remote curb.
notes: Verified 2026-09-27 on the airport's Ground Transportation page (headless browser). Off-airport rental companies (America, Carl's Van, Carwiz, DFG, Florida Van, Easirent, Economy, GreenMotion, OC, One Switch, Priceless, U-Save, Via) pick up by courtesy vehicle at the Rental Car Center remote curb. Peer-to-peer car sharing (Turo) is only permitted in the Economy Parking Garage. Wikipedia: the Rental Car Center opened Feb 14, 2018 with space for 5,300 vehicles. The point is the SkyConnect station from HART's GTFS.

name: Rideshare pickup at Tampa International Airport
summary: At Tampa International Airport, Lyft, Uber and Wridz riders are picked up at the Red Express Curbside, the Blue Express Curbside or the SkyCenter One office building remote curbside, and the airport adds a $5.00 service fee to the fare. Uber's own page says to follow the Blue Express Pickup signs and, with bags, to take the elevator from baggage claim to level 3.
notes: Verified 2026-09-27 on the airport's Ground Transportation page (read in a headless browser). Drop-offs may be at any public access location including Ticketing, Baggage Claim or the SkyCenter One remote curbside. Uber notes the map and zones can change with construction and airport rules. The point is the airport, not the pickup zone.

name: Treasure Island beach parking
fare_text: City lots and spaces: $5.00 an hour Mon-Fri, $5.50 an hour weekends and holidays. Sunset Beach side streets: $6.00 an hour Mon-Fri, $6.50 weekends and holidays. Pay by text or with ParkMobile.
summary: Treasure Island has 24 public parking areas with almost 600 spaces along nearly four miles of beach; beach accesses are marked with blue and orange seagull signs. License-plate readers enforce payment, so backing into spaces is not allowed.

name: Veterans Expressway (SR 589)
fare_text: 2-axle car at the mainline plazas, SunPass / Toll-By-Plate: Anderson Plaza $1.16 / $1.45; Sugarwood Plaza $0.86 / $1.16. Ramp tolls $0.28-$1.16 (SunPass). Rates effective July 1, 2023.
summary: A cashless toll road running north from SR 60 (exit 2A, toward Clearwater) through northwest Hillsborough County to the Suncoast Parkway (exit 13) and Dale Mabry Highway (exit 16); the Suncoast Parkway continues north through Pasco, Hernando and Citrus counties.
